title: Turn And Face The Strange
excerpt: Documentation and guides from the team at Fly.io.
content_html:
We’re Fly.io, a public cloud platform that is both our favorite way to put an app on the Internet and our favorite way to safely let a frontier agent coding harness cook. This is a post about our company, the future, and Sprites, which are computers for agents that you can check out right now.

This is a complicated post. So I need you to promise me something: if you read past this introduction, you’ll read the whole rest of the way through. It’s an honor thing.

A couple months back, Theo Browne ran a video rating the “best place to host a new application in 2026”. Theo tends to say nice things about us. He did this time too. But then he concluded by saying that of all the providers he pays attention to, we were the one he was least confident would be around by the end of the year.

Well, fuck.

Theo startled us, because we’re in the middle of a run of strong quarters that have included the best financial months in the company’s history. But that take has been rattling around in my brain. It whacked me right on a raw nerve, about what we’re doing and where we’re going as a company.

Honestly, I should’ve seen this coming. Fly.io has been motoring along this year, but I’ve coasted a bit, letting the company smolder in an unresolved identity crisis.

I’m going to overshare some more in a second, but I won’t leave you hanging. So: we’ve raised a bunch more money. We’re launching a new iteration of Sprites, and focusing the company on them and the problem they solve. And I’m tagging in Scott Johnston as CEO.

Product-Market Fit

I started Fly.io with two clear principles that probably don’t matter anymore.

The first is that Internet applications work best when they’re fast, and that happens when they’re deployed close to users. I learned this over many years of working at Ars Technica, and started Fly.io in part to scratch an itch. It was our mantra over the first several years of the company.

The second is that cloud infrastructure is too complicated. Developers need platforms with the flexibility of AWS and the ergonomics of Heroku. When we started Fly.io, you couldn’t get both things at the same time, and now you can, here and elsewhere.

You read this and say, “no shit, of course these things are important.” But I’m here to tell you they’re less important than you think, for an obvious reason — the only reason anybody talks about anymore. AI has transmogrified software development. The dingo has truly eaten our baby.

† For the past 18 months, every time I’ve said these words, they’ve gotten even truer.

I don’t think it’s fully sunk in yet[†]. We’re still trying to integrate coding agents into our profession like they’re sufficiently smart compilers. But AI isn’t like the difference between shipping C code and shipping Ruby. It’s much bigger.

Everybody forgets that before Dan Bricklin invented the spreadsheet, every “Excel document” in the world was a computer program, built by a computer programmer. In just a matter of years, every business professional became a programmer, using the world’s most important programming language, spreadsheet formulas. AI is like that, but bigger. Almost anybody will probably be able to build almost any kind of computer program.

Now consider conventional public cloud infrastructure. We take fixed-function applications built to rigorous standards on fussy CI/CD rails and ship them to audiences of millions of people. But a computer program with an audience of millions will soon be like a spreadsheet with an audience of a million readers. They exist! But they’re not the norm.

Betting on an opinionated public cloud design from 2020 is the same as betting against personalized, adaptive software. I don’t think that’s a good bet. And even if I did, I wouldn’t want to make it. I want a world where my friends and family can make computers do exactly what they want, without waiting for me to build everything for them.

What Agents Want

That brings us to our second founding principle, which is that serious cloud infrastructure is too hard for developers to use well. And: still true! But this even more obviously doesn’t matter anymore.

† It is in fact possible that it’s now worse to have a carefully curated human developer experience with opinionated defaults. Agents work best when things are explicit.

To a first approximation, nobody reads documentation anymore. They’re not picking up new CLIs and figuring out how to use them by trial and error, either[†]. That’s what agents are for. An agent can one-shot a Fly.io deployment: just build a site locally and say “now get this working on Fly.io”, and it’ll work great. But an agent can also one-shot an AWS deployment. What are we doing here? What’s going on?

I wrote about this last year, in a post about how our fastest-growing customers were all robots. Then I stopped retconning what we’d already built and got to work figuring out what the robot customers actually want. Here’s what I came up with.

Thing 1: Coding agents expect to run on developer workstations.

Thing 2: Even in a sandbox that you trust, running an agent on your physical dev laptop is annoying, because your laptop stops running when you close the lid. Raise your hand if you’ve walked up or down a flight of stairs with your MacBook open this year. Is your hand down? I’d guess your home doesn’t have stairs. And so people all end up running their agent sandboxes in the cloud.

Thing 3: Public clouds are an irritating place to run agents. We divide servers into “pets” or “cattle”, but for agents, even a herd cow is too much commitment. You want, I don’t know, a semi-disposable cow, a cow that comes into existence exactly when you want it to and sticks around for exactly as long as you want and doesn’t cost very much — and this is why analogies are hard to write.

Earlier this year, our team made what I believe is a breakthrough in systems engineering and perhaps all of computer science: we launched the semi-disposable cow. We call them Sprites.

Sprites take an odd shape that comes from shrink-wrapping them around what I think the robots are looking for. You can create hundreds or thousands of them quickly, but all of them have 100GB durable disk drives. Like everything in the cloud, they have metered utility billing, but the meter doesn’t run when they’re not doing anything, and they’re smart about figuring out when they’re idle. And you can host an app on them and share it with your coworkers, over the Internet.

This grab-bag of features adds up to a proposition about agents. The industry obsesses over sandboxes. But robots don’t want sandboxes. They want computers. That’s what our semi-disposable cow is: a computer for an agent.

Computers For Agents

I’m happy with how the Sprites launch played out. But honestly, Sprites were a skunkworks project. We didn’t even host them on the main Fly.io website! A weird move. I’m not rationalizing it. We were in an identity crisis. But the clouds have parted, and Computers for Agents are, going forward, the focus of our company.

† (to get a flavor of how true that is: a git blame of the whole codebase shows my name more than any other)

Fly Machines and our Platform As A Service features aren’t going anywhere. But Sprites was the product of a tiny skeleton crew inside of Fly.io[†], and now it isn’t.

Ordinarily we’d spend thousands of words on deep-dive technical content about how we built any new product we launched. We’ll do that for Sprites too. But I’m pretty deep into this post already and I have other stuff to share. So for now, I’m going to keep it brief.

In addition to behind-the-scenes work we’ve done on scaling and orchestration, nu-Sprites introduces two big subsystems that get us to a place I’d finally consider “feature-complete” for what we’re trying to do.

The first is the Sprite Block Device (SBD). The original Sprites storage stack was a goblin contraption I personally derived from JuiceFS and wired into our system using Ben Johnson’s Litestream. You should be glad to hear that Ben and Tim Newsham tore that whole stack down to the studs and rebuilt it. It’s faster, more reliable, and still does instant checkpoint-and-restore.

More importantly, SBD enables drive forking: you can create a template Sprite, and then efficiently clone millions of times.

The other big new thing in Sprites is Connectors. Connectors build on work we did to secure our core platform: they let Sprites make authenticated requests to other systems, without giving agents anything useful to exfiltrate. Connectors have fun security properties, but are also much more pleasant to use than manually managing accounts and API keys.

These are our most requested features. They’re the reason so many agent companies are still using Fly Machines many months after we launched a product specifically for them. So I’m confident enough to bet: unless some new space alien technology arrives that does something even weirder to computer science than what Transformer models have done, Sprites are the right fit for our future customers, and a very large portion of our existing ones. Which brings us to:

I Quit

This has been a little while coming, but for the stage Fly.io is at, I think it’s extracted most of the good stuff out of me being CEO. So I’m going to stop doing that.

For the first several years of a startup, you’re running a science project, an experiment-driven search for product-market fit. As anybody who’s worked here can attest, we tried dozens of things, from unmanaged Postgres (never do this) to global CDNs to user-mode WireGuard. Deeper into the company fabric, we built a bottom-up engineering org, avoided product roadmaps, and recruited an all-remote team with members in over a dozen countries.

Some experiments paid off, and others were learning opportunities. Running them has been my whole life over the last 8 years. But Fly.io doesn’t need these kinds of science projects anymore.

For the past many months, stretching way back into 2025, I’ve been talking to Scott Johnston about what Fly.io would look like if he was calling the plays. Scott was the CEO of Docker, and led that through a really challenging time that began with Docker’s own enterprise-vs.-developer identity crisis and ended with them blowing the doors off the business. As a shareholder of Fly.io, for this stage in Fly.io’s lifecycle, I liked his playbook better than mine. As the CEO of Fly.io, I liked the prospect of him doing all this work more than I liked the prospect of me doing it. We took a lot of time to work this out, and ultimately the board and I convinced him to take the job.

This is the paragraph in these kinds of posts where I’m supposed to tell you why Scott is a perfect fit for Fly.io and recount all his past adventures. And he is, and they were majestic. But you already know what I’m going to say here, which makes it boring, and Scott can introduce himself just fine when he wants to. He’s not shy.

Meanwhile, I’m going to do what all the smart spent founder CEOs do, and move to an advisor role parachuting randomly into product design discussions (the fun part of my job) while using my board seat to annoy Scott as he executes what (for me) was the unfun part of my job better than I could have.

One of the things I’m sure Scott will break down is the fundraise we just did. That’s another thing Theo Browne called out in his video (I’m not mad, do I sound mad?) — that we hadn’t announced a raise in several years. The answer to that is: we raised a fuckload of money and didn’t need more. We’ve been operating on the threshold of never needing more, if we stuck to our original plans, and if AI didn’t cause the ground to open up and swallow us all whole. But obviously, that’s no longer the game plan.

Ch-ch-changes

Look, I know how this is going to go over. I could write this post without pissing anybody off, but I don’t know how to do that and still have it be worth reading.

We’re making a very specific and probably polarizing bet on the future of the industry: that agents, within a few years, are going to determine how almost all software is built and shipped. That software is going to become much more personal, with smaller audiences, and much more flexible and slippery.

I’m excited about all of this. I’m a little taken aback that I get to work in this field during a shift like this. But I’d have to be oblivious not to see how uncomfortable that shift makes other professionals in the field.

By the middle of the year, we could have gone one of two ways:

  • On the first path: keep investing our energy in exactly what we’ve been scaling out and refining, a platform for fixed-function full-stack applications designed by humans.
  • On the second path: dial in and nail a product that fits an agent-driven near future of software.

Five of the most dangerous words in startups are “¿Por qué no los dos?”. We do one thing or the other. We don’t limp in on both. And if we fail, we fail with our full asses. Though, I guess only most of mine going forward.

It’s a hell of a thing, steering a team, a company, a base of customers at this stage in Fly.io’s life. We’d been putting off a big decision about priorities for several months. Theo, you picked up on that. Good note! I could have decided quicker, and more clearly; instead, I shipped Sprites. Sprites answer the question that’s been facing us. I’m glad I spent the time building them, and I’m glad we’ve recruited Scott to turn them into our core business.

blocks.html_en: I started Fly.io with two clear principles that probably don’t matter anymore.

sentences.en: I started Fly.io with two clear principles that probably don’t matter anymore.
sentences.zh: 我创立 Fly.io 时有两个明确的原则，但现在可能已经不再重要了。

blocks.html_en: The first is that Internet applications work best when they’re fast, and that happens when they’re deployed close to users. I learned this over many years of working at Ars Technica, and started Fly.io in part to scratch an itch. It was our mantra over the first several years of the company.

sentences.en: The first is that Internet applications work best when they’re fast, and that happens when they’re deployed close to users.
sentences.zh: 首先，互联网应用程序速度快时效果最佳，而且当它们部署在靠近用户的地方时，效果最佳。

sentences.en: I learned this over many years of working at Ars Technica, and started Fly.io in part to scratch an itch.
sentences.zh: 我在 Ars Technica 工作多年后了解到了这一点，并创建了 Fly.io，部分原因是为了解决这个问题。

sentences.en: It was our mantra over the first several years of the company.
sentences.zh: 这是我们公司成立最初几年的座右铭。

blocks.html_en: The second is that cloud infrastructure is too complicated. Developers need platforms with the flexibility of AWS and the ergonomics of Heroku. When we started Fly.io, you couldn’t get both things at the same time, and now you can, here and elsewhere.

sentences.en: The second is that cloud infrastructure is too complicated.
sentences.zh: 二是云基础设施过于复杂。

sentences.en: Developers need platforms with the flexibility of AWS and the ergonomics of Heroku.
sentences.zh: 开发人员需要具有 AWS 灵活性和 Heroku 人体工程学设计的平台。

sentences.en: When we started Fly.io, you couldn’t get both things at the same time, and now you can, here and elsewhere.
sentences.zh: 当我们创办 Fly.io 时，你无法同时获得这两件事，而现在你可以在这里和其他地方同时获得。

blocks.html_en: You read this and say, “no shit, of course these things are important.” But I’m here to tell you they’re less important than you think, for an obvious reason — the only reason anybody talks about anymore. AI has transmogrified software development. The dingo has truly eaten our baby.

sentences.en: You read this and say, “no shit, of course these things are important.”
sentences.zh: 你读到这篇文章后会说：“没什么，这些事情当然很重要。”

sentences.en: But I’m here to tell you they’re less important than you think, for an obvious reason — the only reason anybody talks about anymore.
sentences.zh: 但我来这里是想告诉你，它们并没有你想象的那么重要，原因很明显——这是人们谈论的唯一原因。

sentences.en: AI has transmogrified software development.
sentences.zh: 人工智能已经改变了软件开发。

sentences.en: The dingo has truly eaten our baby.
sentences.zh: 野狗确实吃了我们的孩子。

blocks.html_en: † For the past 18 months, every time I’ve said these words, they’ve gotten even truer.

sentences.en: † For the past 18 months, every time I’ve said these words, they’ve gotten even truer.
sentences.zh: † 在过去的 18 个月里，每当我说出这些话时，它们就变得更加真实。

blocks.html_en: I don’t think it’s fully sunk in yet[†]. We’re still trying to integrate coding agents into our profession like they’re sufficiently smart compilers. But AI isn’t like the difference between shipping C code and shipping Ruby. It’s much bigger.

sentences.en: I don’t think it’s fully sunk in yet[†].
sentences.zh: 我认为它还没有完全融入[†]。

sentences.en: We’re still trying to integrate coding agents into our profession like they’re sufficiently smart compilers.
sentences.zh: 我们仍在尝试将编码代理集成到我们的职业中，就像它们是足够智能的编译器一样。

sentences.en: But AI isn’t like the difference between shipping C code and shipping Ruby.
sentences.zh: 但人工智能并不像发布 C 代码和发布 Ruby 之间的区别。

sentences.en: It’s much bigger.
sentences.zh: 它要大得多。

blocks.html_en: Everybody forgets that before Dan Bricklin invented the spreadsheet, every “Excel document” in the world was a computer program, built by a computer programmer. In just a matter of years, every business professional became a programmer, using the world’s most important programming language, spreadsheet formulas. AI is like that, but bigger. Almost anybody will probably be able to build almost any kind of computer program.

sentences.en: Everybody forgets that before Dan Bricklin invented the spreadsheet, every “Excel document” in the world was a computer program, built by a computer programmer.
sentences.zh: 每个人都忘记了，在 Dan Bricklin 发明电子表格之前，世界上的每个“Excel 文档”都是一个计算机程序，由计算机程序员构建。

sentences.en: In just a matter of years, every business professional became a programmer, using the world’s most important programming language, spreadsheet formulas.
sentences.zh: 在短短几年内，每个商业专业人士都成为了一名程序员，使用世界上最重要的编程语言——电子表格公式。

sentences.en: AI is like that, but bigger.
sentences.zh: 人工智能就是这样，但更大。

sentences.en: Almost anybody will probably be able to build almost any kind of computer program.
sentences.zh: 几乎任何人都可能能够构建几乎任何类型的计算机程序。

blocks.html_en: Now consider conventional public cloud infrastructure. We take fixed-function applications built to rigorous standards on fussy CI/CD rails and ship them to audiences of millions of people. But a computer program with an audience of millions will soon be like a spreadsheet with an audience of a million readers. They exist! But they’re not the norm.

sentences.en: Now consider conventional public cloud infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 现在考虑传统的公共云基础设施。

sentences.en: We take fixed-function applications built to rigorous standards on fussy CI/CD rails and ship them to audiences of millions of people.
sentences.zh: 我们采用在挑剔的 CI/CD 轨道上按照严格标准构建的固定功能应用程序，并将其交付给数百万人的受众。

sentences.en: But a computer program with an audience of millions will soon be like a spreadsheet with an audience of a million readers.
sentences.zh: 但拥有数百万受众的计算机程序很快就会像拥有100万读者的电子表格一样。

sentences.en: They exist!
sentences.zh: 他们存在！

sentences.en: But they’re not the norm.
sentences.zh: 但它们不是常态。

blocks.html_en: Betting on an opinionated public cloud design from 2020 is the same as betting against personalized, adaptive software. I don’t think that’s a good bet. And even if I did, I wouldn’t want to make it. I want a world where my friends and family can make computers do exactly what they want, without waiting for me to build everything for them.

sentences.en: Betting on an opinionated public cloud design from 2020 is the same as betting against personalized, adaptive software.
sentences.zh: 从 2020 年开始，押注于固执己见的公共云设计与押注于个性化、自适应软件是一样的。

sentences.en: I don’t think that’s a good bet.
sentences.zh: 我认为这不是一个好的选择。

sentences.en: And even if I did, I wouldn’t want to make it.
sentences.zh: 即使我做到了，我也不想成功。

sentences.en: I want a world where my friends and family can make computers do exactly what they want, without waiting for me to build everything for them.
sentences.zh: 我想要一个世界，我的朋友和家人可以让计算机完全按照他们的意愿行事，而无需等待我为他们构建一切。

blocks.html_en: What Agents Want

sentences.en: What Agents Want
sentences.zh: 代理商想要什么

blocks.html_en: That brings us to our second founding principle, which is that serious cloud infrastructure is too hard for developers to use well. And: still true! But this even more obviously doesn’t matter anymore.

sentences.en: That brings us to our second founding principle, which is that serious cloud infrastructure is too hard for developers to use well.
sentences.zh: 这就引出了我们的第二个基本原则，即严肃的云基础设施对于开发人员来说太难使用了。

sentences.en: And: still true!
sentences.zh: 并且：仍然如此！

sentences.en: But this even more obviously doesn’t matter anymore.
sentences.zh: 但这显然已经不再重要了。

blocks.html_en: † It is in fact possible that it’s now worse to have a carefully curated human developer experience with opinionated defaults. Agents work best when things are explicit.

sentences.en: † It is in fact possible that it’s now worse to have a carefully curated human developer experience with opinionated defaults.
sentences.zh: † 事实上，现在可能更糟糕的是，精心策划的人类开发者体验和固执己见的默认设置。

sentences.en: Agents work best when things are explicit.
sentences.zh: 当事情明确时，代理工作效果最好。

blocks.html_en: To a first approximation, nobody reads documentation anymore. They’re not picking up new CLIs and figuring out how to use them by trial and error, either[†]. That’s what agents are for. An agent can one-shot a Fly.io deployment: just build a site locally and say “now get this working on Fly.io”, and it’ll work great. But an agent can also one-shot an AWS deployment. What are we doing here? What’s going on?

sentences.en: To a first approximation, nobody reads documentation anymore.
sentences.zh: 初步估计，没有人再阅读文档了。

sentences.en: They’re not picking up new CLIs and figuring out how to use them by trial and error, either[†].
sentences.zh: 他们也没有选择新的 CLI 并通过反复试验来弄清楚如何使用它们[†]。

sentences.en: That’s what agents are for.
sentences.zh: 这就是代理的用途。

sentences.en: An agent can one-shot a Fly.io deployment: just build a site locally and say “now get this working on Fly.io”, and it’ll work great.
sentences.zh: 代理可以一次性部署 Fly.io：只需在本地构建一个站点并说“现在在 Fly.io 上运行它”，它就会工作得很好。

sentences.en: But an agent can also one-shot an AWS deployment.
sentences.zh: 但代理也可以一次性完成 AWS 部署。

sentences.en: What are we doing here?
sentences.zh: 我们在这里做什么？

sentences.en: What’s going on?
sentences.zh: 这是怎么回事？

blocks.html_en: I wrote about this last year, in a post about how our fastest-growing customers were all robots. Then I stopped retconning what we’d already built and got to work figuring out what the robot customers actually want. Here’s what I came up with.

sentences.en: I wrote about this last year, in a post about how our fastest-growing customers were all robots.
sentences.zh: 我去年在一篇关于我们增长最快的客户如何都是机器人的文章中写过这一点。

sentences.en: Then I stopped retconning what we’d already built and got to work figuring out what the robot customers actually want.
sentences.zh: 然后我停止重新审视我们已经构建的内容，并开始弄清楚机器人客户真正想要什么。

sentences.en: Here’s what I came up with.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的想法。

blocks.html_en: Thing 1: Coding agents expect to run on developer workstations.

sentences.en: Thing 1: Coding agents expect to run on developer workstations.
sentences.zh: 第 1 件事：编码代理希望在开发人员工作站上运行。

blocks.html_en: Thing 2: Even in a sandbox that you trust, running an agent on your physical dev laptop is annoying, because your laptop stops running when you close the lid. Raise your hand if you’ve walked up or down a flight of stairs with your MacBook open this year. Is your hand down? I’d guess your home doesn’t have stairs. And so people all end up running their agent sandboxes in the cloud.

sentences.en: Thing 2: Even in a sandbox that you trust, running an agent on your physical dev laptop is annoying, because your laptop stops running when you close the lid.
sentences.zh: 事情 2：即使在您信任的沙箱中，在物理开发笔记本电脑上运行代理也很烦人，因为当您合上盖子时，您的笔记本电脑就会停止运行。

sentences.en: Raise your hand if you’ve walked up or down a flight of stairs with your MacBook open this year.
sentences.zh: 如果您今年曾打开 MacBook 上下楼梯，请举手。

sentences.en: Is your hand down?
sentences.zh: 你的手放下了吗？

sentences.en: I’d guess your home doesn’t have stairs.
sentences.zh: 我猜你家没有楼梯。

sentences.en: And so people all end up running their agent sandboxes in the cloud.
sentences.zh: 因此，人们最终都在云中运行他们的代理沙箱。

blocks.html_en: Thing 3: Public clouds are an irritating place to run agents. We divide servers into “pets” or “cattle”, but for agents, even a herd cow is too much commitment. You want, I don’t know, a semi-disposable cow, a cow that comes into existence exactly when you want it to and sticks around for exactly as long as you want and doesn’t cost very much — and this is why analogies are hard to write.

sentences.en: Thing 3: Public clouds are an irritating place to run agents.
sentences.zh: 第三件事：公共云是运行代理的令人恼火的地方。

sentences.en: We divide servers into “pets” or “cattle”, but for agents, even a herd cow is too much commitment.
sentences.zh: 我们将服务器分为“宠物”或“牛”，但对于代理来说，即使是一头牛也是太多的承诺。

sentences.en: You want, I don’t know, a semi-disposable cow, a cow that comes into existence exactly when you want it to and sticks around for exactly as long as you want and doesn’t cost very much — and this is why analogies are hard to write.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，你想要一头半一次性的奶牛，一头在你想要它出现的时候就出现的奶牛，只要你想要它就可以一直存在，而且成本不高——这就是为什么类比很难写的原因。

blocks.html_en: Earlier this year, our team made what I believe is a breakthrough in systems engineering and perhaps all of computer science: we launched the semi-disposable cow. We call them Sprites.

sentences.en: Earlier this year, our team made what I believe is a breakthrough in systems engineering and perhaps all of computer science: we launched the semi-disposable cow.
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候，我们的团队取得了我认为是系统工程乃至整个计算机科学领域的突破：我们推出了半一次性奶牛。

sentences.en: We call them Sprites.
sentences.zh: 我们称它们为精灵。

blocks.html_en: Sprites take an odd shape that comes from shrink-wrapping them around what I think the robots are looking for. You can create hundreds or thousands of them quickly, but all of them have 100GB durable disk drives. Like everything in the cloud, they have metered utility billing, but the meter doesn’t run when they’re not doing anything, and they’re smart about figuring out when they’re idle. And you can host an app on them and share it with your coworkers, over the Internet.

sentences.en: Sprites take an odd shape that comes from shrink-wrapping them around what I think the robots are looking for.
sentences.zh: 精灵的形状很奇怪，是因为它们被收缩包裹在我认为机器人正在寻找的东西周围。

sentences.en: You can create hundreds or thousands of them quickly, but all of them have 100GB durable disk drives.
sentences.zh: 您可以快速创建数百或数千个，但它们都具有 100GB 耐用磁盘驱动器。

sentences.en: Like everything in the cloud, they have metered utility billing, but the meter doesn’t run when they’re not doing anything, and they’re smart about figuring out when they’re idle.
sentences.zh: 与云中的所有内容一样，他们对公用事业账单进行计量，但当他们不做任何事情时，电表不会运行，并且他们很聪明地判断出他们何时闲置。

sentences.en: And you can host an app on them and share it with your coworkers, over the Internet.
sentences.zh: 您可以在它们上托管一个应用程序，并通过互联网与您的同事共享。

blocks.html_en: This grab-bag of features adds up to a proposition about agents. The industry obsesses over sandboxes. But robots don’t want sandboxes. They want computers. That’s what our semi-disposable cow is: a computer for an agent.

sentences.en: This grab-bag of features adds up to a proposition about agents.
sentences.zh: 这些功能组合在一起构成了一个关于代理的命题。

sentences.en: The industry obsesses over sandboxes.
sentences.zh: 该行业对沙箱非常着迷。

sentences.en: But robots don’t want sandboxes.
sentences.zh: 但机器人不需要沙箱。

sentences.en: They want computers.
sentences.zh: 他们想要电脑。

sentences.en: That’s what our semi-disposable cow is: a computer for an agent.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们的半一次性牛：代理的计算机。

sentences.zh: 我们甚至没有在 Fly.io 主网站上托管它们！

sentences.en: I’m not rationalizing it.

sentences.en: We were in an identity crisis.

sentences.en: But the clouds have parted, and Computers for Agents are, going forward, the focus of our company.
sentences.zh: 但云已经散去，面向代理的计算机是我们公司未来的重点。

blocks.html_en: Fly Machines and our Platform As A Service features aren’t going anywhere. But Sprites was the product of a tiny skeleton crew inside of Fly.io[†], and now it isn’t.

sentences.en: Fly Machines and our Platform As A Service features aren’t going anywhere.
sentences.zh: Fly Machines 和我们的平台即服务功能不会消失。

sentences.en: But Sprites was the product of a tiny skeleton crew inside of Fly.io[†], and now it isn’t.
sentences.zh: 但 Sprites 是 Fl​​y.io[†] 内部一小群骨干人员的产物，但现在不是了。

blocks.html_en: Ordinarily we’d spend thousands of words on deep-dive technical content about how we built any new product we launched. We’ll do that for Sprites too. But I’m pretty deep into this post already and I have other stuff to share. So for now, I’m going to keep it brief.

sentences.en: Ordinarily we’d spend thousands of words on deep-dive technical content about how we built any new product we launched.
sentences.zh: 通常，我们会花费数千字来深入探讨我们如何构建我们推出的新产品的技术内容。

sentences.en: We’ll do that for Sprites too.
sentences.zh: 我们也会为 Sprites 做同样的事情。

sentences.en: But I’m pretty deep into this post already and I have other stuff to share.
sentences.zh: 但我已经很深入地研究了这篇文章，并且我还有其他东西要分享。

sentences.en: So for now, I’m going to keep it brief.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，我将保持简短。

blocks.html_en: In addition to behind-the-scenes work we’ve done on scaling and orchestration, nu-Sprites introduces two big subsystems that get us to a place I’d finally consider “feature-complete” for what we’re trying to do.

sentences.en: In addition to behind-the-scenes work we’ve done on scaling and orchestration, nu-Sprites introduces two big subsystems that get us to a place I’d finally consider “feature-complete” for what we’re trying to do.
sentences.zh: 除了我们在扩展和编排方面所做的幕后工作之外，nu-Sprites 还引入了两个大型子系统，这些子系统使我们达到了一个我最终认为我们正在尝试做的事情“功能完整”的地方。

blocks.html_en: The first is the Sprite Block Device (SBD). The original Sprites storage stack was a goblin contraption I personally derived from JuiceFS and wired into our system using Ben Johnson’s Litestream. You should be glad to hear that Ben and Tim Newsham tore that whole stack down to the studs and rebuilt it. It’s faster, more reliable, and still does instant checkpoint-and-restore.

sentences.en: The first is the Sprite Block Device (SBD).
sentences.zh: 第一个是 Sprite 块设备 (SBD)。

sentences.en: The original Sprites storage stack was a goblin contraption I personally derived from JuiceFS and wired into our system using Ben Johnson’s Litestream.
sentences.zh: 最初的 Sprites 存储堆栈是我个人从 JuiceFS 衍生出来的一个妖精装置，并使用 Ben Johnson 的 Litestream 连接到我们的系统中。

sentences.en: You should be glad to hear that Ben and Tim Newsham tore that whole stack down to the studs and rebuilt it.
sentences.zh: 你应该很高兴听到 Ben 和 Tim Newsham 将整个堆栈拆除并重建。

sentences.en: It’s faster, more reliable, and still does instant checkpoint-and-restore.
sentences.zh: 它更快、更可靠，并且仍然可以进行即时检查点和恢复。

blocks.html_en: More importantly, SBD enables drive forking: you can create a template Sprite, and then efficiently clone millions of times.

sentences.en: More importantly, SBD enables drive forking: you can create a template Sprite, and then efficiently clone millions of times.
sentences.zh: 更重要的是，SBD 支持驱动分叉：您可以创建模板 Sprite，然后高效地克隆数百万次。

blocks.html_en: The other big new thing in Sprites is Connectors. Connectors build on work we did to secure our core platform: they let Sprites make authenticated requests to other systems, without giving agents anything useful to exfiltrate. Connectors have fun security properties, but are also much more pleasant to use than manually managing accounts and API keys.

sentences.en: The other big new thing in Sprites is Connectors.

content_html_zh:
我们是 Fly.io，一个公共云平台，它既是我们最喜欢的将应用程序放在互联网上的方式，也是我们最喜欢的安全地让前沿代理编码工具烹饪的方式。 这是一篇关于我们公司、未来和 Sprites 的文章，Sprites 是供代理使用的计算机，您现在就可以查看。

这是一篇复杂的帖子。 所以我需要你向我保证一件事：如果你读完这篇介绍，你就会读完剩下的内容。 这是一件荣幸的事情。

几个月前，Theo Browne 发布了一段视频，将其评为“2026 年托管新应用程序的最佳地点”。 西奥经常说我们的好话。 这次他也这么做了。 但他最后表示，在他关注的所有提供商中，我们是他最没有信心在今年年底之前出现的提供商。

好吧，他妈的。

西奥让我们吃了一惊，因为我们正处于一系列强劲的季度之中，其中包括公司历史上最好的财务月份。 但这个想法一直在我的脑海里盘旋。 作为一家公司，我们正在做什么以及我们将走向何方，这让我感到非常震惊。

老实说，我应该预见到这一点。 今年 Fly.io 一路高歌猛进，但我却稍稍放慢了脚步，让该公司在未解决的身份危机中郁郁不得志。

我稍后会分享更多内容，但我不会让你悬而未决。 所以：我们筹集了更多资金。 我们正在推出 Sprites 的新版本，并将公司的重点放在它们和它们解决的问题上。 我任命斯科特·约翰斯顿为首席执行官。

产品与市场契合度

我创立 Fly.io 时有两个明确的原则，但现在可能已经不再重要了。

首先，互联网应用程序速度快时效果最佳，而且当它们部署在靠近用户的地方时，效果最佳。 我在 Ars Technica 工作多年后了解到了这一点，并创建了 Fly.io，部分原因是为了解决这个问题。 这是我们公司成立最初几年的座右铭。

二是云基础设施过于复杂。 开发人员需要具有 AWS 灵活性和 Heroku 人体工程学设计的平台。 当我们创办 Fly.io 时，你无法同时获得这两件事，而现在你可以在这里和其他地方同时获得。

你读到这篇文章后会说：“没什么，这些事情当然很重要。” 但我来这里是想告诉你，它们并没有你想象的那么重要，原因很明显——这是人们谈论的唯一原因。 人工智能已经改变了软件开发。 野狗确实吃了我们的孩子。

† 在过去的 18 个月里，每当我说出这些话时，它们就变得更加真实。

我认为它还没有完全融入[†]。 我们仍在尝试将编码代理集成到我们的职业中，就像它们是足够智能的编译器一样。 但人工智能并不像发布 C 代码和发布 Ruby 之间的区别。 它要大得多。

每个人都忘记了，在 Dan Bricklin 发明电子表格之前，世界上的每个“Excel 文档”都是一个计算机程序，由计算机程序员构建。 在短短几年内，每个商业专业人士都成为了一名程序员，使用世界上最重要的编程语言——电子表格公式。 人工智能就是这样，但更大。 几乎任何人都可能能够构建几乎任何类型的计算机程序。

现在考虑传统的公共云基础设施。 我们采用在挑剔的 CI/CD 轨道上按照严格标准构建的固定功能应用程序，并将其交付给数百万人的受众。 但拥有数百万受众的计算机程序很快就会像拥有100万读者的电子表格一样。 他们存在！ 但它们不是常态。

从 2020 年开始，押注于固执己见的公共云设计与押注于个性化、自适应软件是一样的。 我认为这不是一个好的选择。 即使我做到了，我也不想成功。 我想要一个世界，我的朋友和家人可以让计算机完全按照他们的意愿行事，而无需等待我为他们构建一切。

代理商想要什么

这就引出了我们的第二个基本原则，即严肃的云基础设施对于开发人员来说太难使用了。 并且：仍然如此！ 但这显然已经不再重要了。

† 事实上，现在可能更糟糕的是，精心策划的人类开发者体验和固执己见的默认设置。 当事情明确时，代理工作效果最好。

初步估计，没有人再阅读文档了。 他们也没有选择新的 CLI 并通过反复试验来弄清楚如何使用它们[†]。 这就是代理的用途。 代理可以一次性部署 Fly.io：只需在本地构建一个站点并说“现在在 Fly.io 上运行它”，它就会工作得很好。 但代理也可以一次性完成 AWS 部署。 我们在这里做什么？ 这是怎么回事？

我去年在一篇关于我们增长最快的客户如何都是机器人的文章中写过这一点。 然后我停止重新审视我们已经构建的内容，并开始弄清楚机器人客户真正想要什么。 这就是我的想法。

第 1 件事：编码代理希望在开发人员工作站上运行。

事情 2：即使在您信任的沙箱中，在物理开发笔记本电脑上运行代理也很烦人，因为当您合上盖子时，您的笔记本电脑就会停止运行。 如果您今年曾打开 MacBook 上下楼梯，请举手。 你的手放下了吗？ 我猜你家没有楼梯。 因此，人们最终都在云中运行他们的代理沙箱。

第三件事：公共云是运行代理的令人恼火的地方。 我们将服务器分为“宠物”或“牛”，但对于代理来说，即使是一头牛也是太多的承诺。 我不知道，你想要一头半一次性的奶牛，一头在你想要它出现的时候就出现的奶牛，只要你想要它就可以一直存在，而且成本不高——这就是为什么类比很难写的原因。

今年早些时候，我们的团队取得了我认为是系统工程乃至整个计算机科学领域的突破：我们推出了半一次性奶牛。 我们称它们为精灵。

精灵的形状很奇怪，是因为它们被收缩包裹在我认为机器人正在寻找的东西周围。 您可以快速创建数百或数千个，但它们都具有 100GB 耐用磁盘驱动器。 与云中的所有内容一样，他们对公用事业账单进行计量，但当他们不做任何事情时，电表不会运行，并且他们很聪明地判断出他们何时闲置。 您可以在它们上托管一个应用程序，并通过互联网与您的同事共享。

这些功能组合在一起构成了一个关于代理的命题。 该行业对沙箱非常着迷。 但机器人不需要沙箱。 他们想要电脑。 这就是我们的半一次性牛：代理的计算机。

代理计算机

我对 Sprites 的发布效果感到满意。 但老实说，Sprites 是一个臭鼬工厂项目。 我们甚至没有在 Fly.io 主网站上托管它们！ 一个奇怪的举动。 我并没有合理化它。 我们陷入了身份危机。 但云已经散去，面向代理的计算机是我们公司未来的重点。

除了我们在扩展和编排方面所做的幕后工作之外，nu-Sprites 还引入了两个大型子系统，这些子系统使我们达到了一个我最终认为我们正在尝试做的事情“功能完整”的地方。

第一个是 Sprite 块设备 (SBD)。 最初的 Sprites 存储堆栈是我个人从 JuiceFS 衍生出来的一个妖精装置，并使用 Ben Johnson 的 Litestream 连接到我们的系统中。 你应该很高兴听到 Ben 和 Tim Newsham 将整个堆栈拆除并重建。 它更快、更可靠，并且仍然可以进行即时检查点和恢复。

更重要的是，SBD 支持驱动分叉：您可以创建模板 Sprite，然后高效地克隆数百万次。

Sprites 中的另一个重大新事物是连接器。 连接器建立在我们为保护核心平台所做的工作之上：它们让 Sprites 向其他系统发出经过身份验证的请求，而不会给代理提供任何有用的信息。 连接器具有有趣的安全属性，但也比手动管理帐户和 API 密钥更易于使用。

I Quit

虽然这一切已经过去了一段时间，但就 Fly.io 所处的阶段而言，我认为它已经从我担任首席执行官的过程中汲取了大部分的好东西。 所以我要停止这样做了。

在初创公司的头几年，你正在运行一个科学项目，一个以实验为导向的产品市场契合度搜索。 任何在这里工作过的人都可以证明，我们尝试了很多东西，从非托管 Postgres（永远不要这样做）到全球 CDN，再到用户模式 ​​WireGuard。 在公司结构的更深处，我们建立了一个自下而上的工程组织，避免了产品路线图，并招募了一个成员遍布十多个国家的全远程团队。

一些实验得到了回报，另一些则是学习的机会。 过去 8 年里，经营它们就是我的全部生活。 但 Fly.io 不再需要此类科学项目。

在这类帖子中，我应该在这一段中告诉您为什么 Scott 非常适合 Fly.io，并讲述他过去的所有冒险经历。 他是，而且他们很威严。 但你已经知道我要在这里说什么，这使得它变得无聊，斯科特可以在他想要的时候自我介绍。 他并不害羞。

与此同时，我将做所有聪明的创始人首席执行官所做的事情，并担任顾问角色，随机跳伞进入产品设计讨论（我工作中有趣的部分），同时利用我的董事会席位来惹恼斯科特，因为他比我更好地执行了（对我来说）我工作中不有趣的部分。

初创公司中最危险的五个词是“¿Por qué no los dos?”。 我们做一件事或另一件事。 我们不会在这两方面都陷入困境。 如果我们失败了，我们就会彻底失败。 不过，我想只有我的大部分才能继续前进。

在 Fly.io 生命的这个阶段，领导一个团队、一家公司、一个客户群，这是一件了不起的事情。 我们已经推迟了几个月才做出关于优先事项的重大决定。 西奥，你明白了。 好注意！ 我本可以更快、更清楚地做出决定；相反，我运送了 Sprites。 精灵回答了我们一直面临的问题。 我很高兴我花时间构建它们，我很高兴我们聘请了斯科特将它们变成我们的核心业务。
